title.narrative: Activity under preparation Partnership for Green Energy Transition in Bangladesh - Top Up

description.narrative: The action focuses on the Global Gateway priority ¿Climate and Energy¿ and aims at further strengthening EU action in the area of the Green Energy Transition in Bangladesh. The EU already strongly promotes renewable energy, including through the Bangladesh Renewable Energy Facility. The action has two mutually complementary components. The first component will further strengthen the EU¿s support for enhancing energy efficiency. The second component aims at further strengthening the Team Europe Iniatitive (TEI) on Climate and Energy, including the policy dialogue. This includes the development of Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategies (LT-LEDS) required by the Paris Agreement, the implementation of the updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and National Adaptation Plan (NAP), which are essential to both the energy transition and to strengthening climate resilience. In 2025, the successful Team Europe Initiative on the Green Energy Transition was broadened to a Team Europe Initiative on Climate and Energy. This broader scope better reflects the ¿climate change¿ dimension of the Global Gateway priority, aligns with Member States¿ growing focus on climate adaptation - identified through a comprehensive mapping exercise - and responds to Bangladesh¿s needs as one of the world¿s most climate-vulnerable countries. The action intends to contribute to both specific objectives under the MIP 2021-27 Priority Area 2 - Green Inclusive Development, i.e. Specific Objective 1 ¿to promote energy efficiency and affordable renewable energy¿ and Specific Objective 2 ¿to improve environmental protection and support climate change mitigation and adaptation in Bangladesh¿s sustainable development¿. The two components both strengthen the existing ¿Partnership for Green Energy Transition in Bangladesh¿ project (AAP 2022, implemented by GIZ), as follows: Energy EfficiencyThe action will support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 7 on Affordable and Clean Energy, including the policy dialogue on the definition and implementation of sectoral and national energy efficiency targets, which are essential for future investments in energy efficiency. In the interest of the competitiveness of the European private sector, the dialogue will focus on sharing European expertise, best practices and standards, in line with the Energy Efficiency First principle and the global energy efficiency pledge, which has been signed by Bangladesh. The action focuses inter alia on industry, including the ready-made garment (RMG) sector, as well as buildings (including air conditioning), thereby also ensuring synergy with the EUR 20 million green construction project (AAP 2023, EUR 10 million from the EU and 10 million from Germany). The action will contribute to the policy dialogue by generating bottom-up implementation evidence, strengthening regulatory enforcement capacities including of the Sustainable and Renewable Energy Authority, improving monitoring and verification systems, and demonstrating scalable implementation and financing models, drawing on European expertise, technologies and best practices. The action will support stronger linkages between European and Bangladeshi companies and help foster increased European investment in both the industrial and building sectors. By fostering regulatory convergence and performance-based markets, the action will reduce barriers for high-efficiency European technologies, while supporting Bangladesh in embedding Energy Efficiency First principles in power systems and demand-side planning.
